newsitem.title: BRAZIL: LatAm shrs seen flat on local issues, U.S. vote.
newsitem.headline: LatAm shrs seen flat on local issues, U.S. vote.

text.p: Equities in most Latin American markets are seen flat to cautiously higher this week, with investors looking to domestic factors and closely monitoring Wall Street after Tuesday's U.S. presidential elections, analysts said.
In Argentina, stocks were expected to keep a positive bias but were likely to track the Dow Industrials amid investor anxiety over the U.S. elections.
"Investors are likely to keep their wait-and-see attitude, with very little volume and sluggish trade in the heavyweight stocks," said Jorge Napoli, of brokers Ignoto y Napoli.
After posting losses for two weeks, the blue-chip Merval index .MERV rebounded 2.6 percent last week to 573.90 points.
Brazilian shares were seen stable to slightly higher as investors await October's export figures and the bid terms for the upcoming privatization of Band B cellular services due out this week.

The Industry and Commerce Ministry is expected to announce exports for the whole month of October Tuesday and analysts said the figures may confirm new market estimates that Brazil's trade deficit will be lower than previously expected.
Analysts now forecast October's trade gap at around $800 million, below previous estimates of a deficit of up to $1.5 billion.
Last week, the Bovespa index .BVSP of the 49 most traded shares gained 2.1 percent to 66,412 points.
In Venezuela, equities are also expected to remain flat, with investor attention focused on the upcoming global share offering of telephone company CANTV.
"Investors have temporarily deserted Caracas, foreigners in particular. They are all awaiting the sale of CANTV," one trader said.
The privatization of CANTV will see 40 percent of the company's stock placed on local and foreign markets. The share price is expected to be announced on November 21.
Stock prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange closed up 0.42 percent at 5,912.86 points.
Analysts also noted this week will be a four-day week for Venezuelan markets as today is a national holiday in observance of All Saints' Day.
Mexican equities are also seen moving with eyes on U.S. elections and prospects for Mexico's economic policy in 1997.
Last week, the market ended up 0.68 percent at 3,255.82 points.
Analysts said expectations over the U.S. elections and the Mexican economy should keep trading volumes at low levels this week, but the bolsa's index could consolidate slightly above 3,250 points.
